gates.test @openpacker/opm-project: pass (217 tests; was 214 — added 3: recorded bins activated without discovery, legacy member discovery fallback, malformed stored bins fail closed)
gates.test @openpacker/opm: pass (26 tests; the bound-project test now also runs the tool both ways)

notes: DEFECT FIXED: project-level `opmx <bin>` for plugin-served packages. Root cause was as reported in layer 04: activateGeneration re-derived bins via discoverBins(storePath, ecosystem), which returns [] for plugin ecosystems, discarding the provider-declared bins pinned in the lock at install. RULE IMPLEMENTED (recorded vs derived): GenerationMember gains optional `bins` — the declared bins the install wrote shims for, recorded by recordGeneration from the installed state record (minus derived shim/target paths, which activation re-derives). activateGeneration uses the recorded bins whenever the member carries them; discoverBins(storePath, ecosystem) runs only when the field is ABSENT, which is exactly the generations recorded before bins were pinned — so legacy records and npm/pypi/nuget discovery semantics are byte-for-byte today's behavior. An explicitly empty recorded array means the package genuinely had no bins and is honored (indistinguishable from discovery anyway, since the store tree is digest-pinned and discovery is deterministic over it). No lock consultation at activation: generations stay self-sufficient, so rollback after the lock moved on still works. INTEGRITY: bins ride inside the digest-verified member record (generationDigest covers members; contentKey dedup unchanged); parseGeneration now fails closed INVALID_STATE on malformed member bins (non-array, non-string/empty name, unsafe name segment, escaping/absolute path, unknown interpreter, non-string entry) — an unknown interpreter must never silently become Node. validateProjectState preserves and validates interpreter/entry on state bins exactly as the lockfile parser does, so a state round-trip (multi-package installs) cannot strip how a bin runs before recordGeneration sees it. SECOND FIX (same run path, apps/opm): the opmx project path spawned every resolved target through process.execPath (Node) — fine for npm, a deferred crash for native/python/dotnet bins. It now dispatches through the same spawnDeclared interpreter switch as ephemeral runs (projectRoot sandbox context preserved), falling back to the old target-spawn only for bins with no owning package record (direct bin-dir path). E2E PROVEN (bwrap-enforced, unified plugin fixture): in a [plugins.<id>]-bound project, opm add pkg:acme/demo@1.0.0 pins the declared native bin into opm.lock.json, state, and .opm/bin; `opmx acme-demo` and `opmx --package demo --bin acme-demo` both exit 0 with stdout 'acme-demo-ran'. REGRESSION: all pre-existing opm-project (214) and opm (25) tests pass unmodified.
deviations: Scope said packages/opm-project primarily with apps/opm tests to prove the fix; proving the e2e required a small runtime change in apps/opm/src/opmx.ts (interpreter-aware dispatch on the project path) — without it the native bin resolves but is run through Node and fails. This also repairs the previously-broken project-level runs of pypi console scripts and nuget tools (they too were spawned through Node); first-party npm behavior is unchanged (interpreter absent → Node, same target). Side effect to be aware of: project python bins now genuinely invoke python3 with all store roots on sys.path, matching the ephemeral path. The pre-existing ephemeral cache defect (fetchTool never hits the store archive, reported in layer 04) remains out of scope and untouched. docs/plans/plugin-execution/ was untracked since layer 01; committed now with the state file's layer-05 row.
